quizzes.stem: Scenario S4, developer productivity with Claude. After two hours on a payments codebase, the agent answers a question about retries by describing how such systems typically retry, though it read the actual retry classes an hour earlier. Which practice would have prevented this?

options.a: Writing specific findings to a notes file and consulting it for later queries
options.b: Switching to a model with a bigger context window for the whole of the session
options.c: Raising the output limit so that each answer can quote more of the code
options.d: Telling the agent in its prompt to avoid generic answers from here onward

explanation.a: The specifics are kept in a file that outlives the window and are read again when a later question needs them.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "A reminder in the prompt does not bring back a class that has left the window".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "a bigger window only moves the problem later".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the symptom is that "answers become inconsistent from one turn to the next, and specific names give way to plausible generalities", which more output does not repair.

quizzes.stem: Scenario S4, developer productivity with Claude. A coordinator must list every test file that covers refunds in a very large repository, then trace the refund flow. It does both in its own conversation, and the context fills with listings and file contents. Which structure fits?

options.a: Hand the whole job to one helper with the brief to explore everything and report it all
options.b: Keep the reading in the coordinator and add a notes file for what it finds
options.c: Give each question to a read-only exploring helper and keep just the summaries
options.d: Use a helper with every tool, so that it can save the lists to files

explanation.c: Each narrow question goes to a read-only subagent, and the coordinator receives only a summary.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "a broad brief returns a broad report".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Each file read, each search result, each command output stays in the window", so the coordinator's own reading keeps filling it.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Read-only matters: an exploration that can edit can also damage".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S4, developer productivity with Claude. During a long exploration the team wants automatic summarising near the limit to keep the roster of sources already opened and the commands that run the tests. What should they do?

options.a: Turn automatic summarising off so that nothing is condensed at all
options.b: Add a sentence on what to preserve to the project's instructions file
options.c: Raise the output limit so that the summary can run longer than usual
options.d: Clear the conversation at each phase so that nothing needs preserving

explanation.b: A standing instruction in the project's file steers the automatic summary toward what the exploration needs.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Turning compaction off is not a remedy: the window then fills, and performance degrades".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Left to itself the summary keeps what looks important", and a longer summary still chooses by that.
explanation.d: Ruled out because clearing "starts over and is right between unrelated tasks", and a phase of the same exploration is not one.

quizzes.stem: Scenario S4, developer productivity with Claude. A coordinator restarts after a crash. Its manifest lists 6 agents as running, and notes written by only 4 of them can be found on disk. What should it do?

options.a: Restart the whole set, since a manifest written before a crash cannot be trusted
options.b: Resume each of the 6 on the manifest's word, giving empty notes to the 2 without any
options.c: Replay the 6 transcripts into the new coordinator before it continues
options.d: Carry on from the saved material where it exists and begin afresh where it does not

explanation.d: The agents with files continue from them and the others start over, since the file outranks the status.
explanation.a: Ruled out because for an agent whose file survived, "the file is there, so the work is kept".
explanation.b: Ruled out because for a missing file there is "nothing to continue from, whatever the manifest says".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "the transcripts are what filled the window".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S4, developer productivity with Claude. After a crash, one agent is started again from material it wrote out earlier. What should its new prompt hold?

options.a: Its assignment alone, because the saved material is implied by it
options.b: Its assignment and the complete old transcript, so that nothing is lost
options.c: Its assignment, the exported notes and an instruction to continue
options.d: The saved notes alone, because the assignment is contained in them

explanation.c: The page says the prompt "carries its task, the state lines it exported, and one instruction: continue from the first unfinished step".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "It does not get the old transcript, which is what filled the first window".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the prompt "carries its task, the state lines it exported", so the notes are not implied.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the prompt "carries its task, the state lines it exported", and the task comes first.

quizzes.stem: Scenario S4, developer productivity with Claude. A team needs a code-searching helper whose work can be picked up later in the same session. Which fits?

options.a: The built-in Explore subagent, continued with its own history
options.b: A custom subagent, continued with its own history
options.c: A fresh Explore each time, handed a copy of the earlier transcript
options.d: A second coordinator that reads the first coordinator's conversation

explanation.b: A custom subagent can be resumed with its history, and the built-in one cannot.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "The built-in Explore agent is one-shot".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "the transcripts are what filled the window".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "a crash that ended the session leaves only the files", and an ordinary session leaves a resumable subagent.

quizzes.stem: Scenario S4, developer productivity with Claude. A session finishes one exploration, and an unrelated piece of work then begins in the same window. Which step fits?

options.a: Turn compaction off for the new job so that no detail is lost
options.b: Compact it with instructions to keep everything the first job found
options.c: Enlarge the context limit so that both jobs fit side by side
options.d: Clear the conversation, since nothing from the first job is needed

explanation.d: The page says "`/clear` starts over and is right between unrelated tasks".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Compaction continues the same work with a shorter memory of it".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "a bigger window only moves the problem later".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Turning compaction off is not a remedy: the window then fills, and performance degrades".
